subject: Stellum: proposed rate split + SOW sequencing
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@stellum.ai>, Contracts <contracts@stellum.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stellum: proposed rate split + SOW sequencing

Hi Sarah / Contracts team —

Thanks for sending the draft SOW and order form. We reviewed the redlines and there are two items we think will materially affect implementation sequencing and billing cadence, so wanted to propose an explicit approach to avoid a long back-and-forth:

1) Rate split for initial ramp (Q1-Q2): Stellum proposed a blended rate. To protect both sides during the pilot we propose a 60/40 split for committed GPU units between implementation and production in months 1–3, with the remainder billed as consumption. This lets you get priority provisioning while limiting Redwood exposure on initial provisioning.

2) SOW sequencing and acceptance triggers: The SOW currently lists a single acceptance gate at deployment. We recommend splitting acceptance into two milestones: (a) integration & smoke tests (ops sign-off) and (b) production acceptance (performance SLA checks). Each milestone would unlock a portion of the implementation fee and trigger billing transition rules in the order form.

Questions for you: can you confirm whether Stellum is okay with milestone-based acceptance? Also, on the billing side, will Stellum accept proration for the month where the split changes (we propose pro-rate based on calendar days)?

Attached are: 1) a marked SOW showing where we'd add the milestones (Stellum_SOW_v2.pdf), and 2) a short redlines doc with the proposed rate split wording (redlines_stellum.docx).

Next steps we suggest:
- Contracts: review the milestone language and confirm if acceptable for Stellum legal.
- Ops: once legal gives a thumbs-up, we'll schedule a 30-min alignment call to map milestones to runbook items.

I'll leave Laura and Aditya on thread for legal and finance sign-off items.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Stellum_SOW_v2.pdf (annotated), redlines_stellum.docx (proposed clause wording)

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@stellum.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Contracts <contracts@stellum.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@stellum.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stellum: proposed rate split + SOW sequencing

Hi Lukas —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the annotated SOW. Quick responses below:

- Milestone acceptance: Stellum is open to splitting acceptance into two gates as you suggested, provided the performance SLA thresholds for production acceptance are explicit in the SOW. Can you add the specific latency/throughput targets you expect ops to validate?

- Proration: We generally prefer calendar-day proration; that should be fine if the order form language is explicit.

I've looped in Tom from our infrastructure team and contracts mailbox. Tom — can you confirm if the 60/40 split for the initial three months will be operationally achievable from a provisioning standpoint? We need to ensure reserved nodes map to our capacity planning.

Legal note: our contracts team will review redlines but expects to remove any one-sided indemnity language. We'll send back a clean tracked copy by Monday.

Thanks,
Sarah Li
Head of Platform Partnerships
Stellum AI

Thanks Sarah — good to hear you're aligned on the two gates. A couple of quick clarifications from commercial: 

- Proposed financial carve: for the 60/40 split we suggest the 60% for reserved capacity be invoiced at the committed rate and the 40% (implementation) be captured as an implementation line item on the order form, invoiced on milestone (a) and (b) as Lukas suggested.
- If production SLA isn't met at milestone (b) we need a limited rollback provision that reclassifies a portion of the reserved capacity back to consumption billing for the first 30 days post-deployment. This avoids customers paying reserved fees while performance is subpar.

Laura / Aditya: can you confirm the rollback clause is acceptable from legal/finance perspectives? If fine, I'll fold into the order form redline and send the clean tracked copy to Stellum.

Karthik
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Stellum: proposed rate split + SOW sequencing

Sarah / Karthik / Lukas —

I've reviewed the proposed milestone split, the 60/40 commercial structure and the suggested rollback language. High-level legal position below: 

1) Milestone wording: acceptable with clarified metrics. Please insert numeric SLA thresholds (p50 latency < 150ms, 99th < 800ms under stated load profile) and a clear test plan in Exhibit B. Without metrics the acceptance gate is subjective.

2) Rollback provision: we can include a 30-day provisional reclass clause limited to up to 25% of the reserved units if production SLA is not met at milestone (b). The clause must specify notice procedures, remediation window, and that reclassification is applied only for billing (not to retroactively change prior payments).

3) Indemnity and liability: Stellum's redlines removed some indemnity limits. We propose mutual indemnities and maintain Redwood's existing liability cap language with carveouts for gross negligence.

4) Implementation invoicing: implementation line items may be invoiced per milestone; however, finance requests payment terms of Net 30 for implementation invoices to keep AR consistent with our practice. Please confirm Stellum is okay with Net 30.

If Stellum agrees, Redwood can produce a consolidated tracked document and a DocuSign envelope for signature. Karthik — once you confirm commercial numbers (final % split and exact fees), I'll prepare the legal redline for final review.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
